entries.title: Ezekiel 17:1
segments:
vv 1-16. 
 
Every covenant which we make with others in lawful things must be faithfully kept, though they be wicked and unreasonable men, and though it seem greatly for our present interest to break our word.  God will listen to no plea of expediency, but will punish perfidy towards our fellow men as falsehood to himself; for he is the God of truth, and demands of us truth in all our dealings.

entries.title: Ezekiel 17:3
segments:
A great eagle; Nebuchadnezzar. 
 
  The highest branch of the cedar; Jehoiachin, whom Nebuchadnezzar dethroned and carried to Babylon.

entries.title: Ezekiel 17:4
segments:
A land of traffic; Chaldea. 
 
  A city of merchants; Babylon.

entries.title: Ezekiel 17:5
segments: Of the seed of the land; that is, of "the king's seed,"
, meaning Zedekiah, son of Josiah, whom Nebuchadnezzar made king in the place of Jehoiachin.  See the narrative,

entries.title: Ezekiel 17:6
segments: Of low stature; not a lofty cedar, as before, but a low vine; that is, a tributary king.  Compare

. 
 
  Turned towrd him; towards Nebuchadnezzar, as dependent upon him.

entries.title: Ezekiel 17:7
segments:
Another great eagle; Pharaoh. 
 
  Did bend her roots toward him; turning away its confidence from Nebuchadnezzar to Pharaoh.

entries.title: Ezekiel 17:9
segments:
Shall he not pull; that is, the first eagle. 
 
  All the leaves of her spring; literally, all the fresh leaves of her springing; that is, all her fresh and green foliage. 
 
  Without great power--roots thereof; or without [the employment of] great power and many people to pluck her up from her roots.  The work of plucking up the vine of Judah from the place where it grew shall not require a numerous force.

entries.title: Ezekiel 17:10
segments: The east wind; a symbol of the Chaldean invasion, bringing with it desolation.

entries.title: Ezekiel 17:13
segments: Taken the mighty of the land; taken them away to Babylon.

entries.title: Ezekiel 17:16
segments: In the midst of Babylon he shall die;

entries.title: Ezekiel 17:17
segments:
vv 17-21. 
 
They who violate their obligations to God and their fellow men, in the hope of some present advantage, generally meet with disappointment and shame in the present life, and they must incur God's wrath and curse in the life to come.

entries.title: Ezekiel 17:22
segments:
Of the highest branch of the high cedar--a tender one; the Messiah, as the context shows, who is here, as elsewhere, compared to a branch of God's planting. 
 
vv 22-24. 
 
God exalts and abases earthly kingdoms as he chooses; but his kingdom of grace stands fast amid all the changes of time, and shall in the end cover the world with its glory.

entries.title: Ezekiel 17:24
segments:
Brought down the high tree; abased Zedekiah and his princes, who are here the representatives of all who exalt themselves against God. 
 
  Exalted the low tree--made the dry tree to flourish; that is, exalted athe Messiah in his stead.  Compare
